drivingQuestion: Is there any boiled vegetable that can be a person's primary sustenance, as Rabbi Akiva's ruling assumes?
outcomeNote: Rav Ashi's restriction to a cabbage stalk removes the difficulty and stands unchallenged.

segments.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ אָכַל שֶׁלֶק כּוּ׳: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה שֶׁלֶק מְזוֹנֵי? אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּקֶלַח שֶׁל כְּרוּב שָׁנוּ.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «Rabbi Akiva says: Even» if «one ate boiled vegetables, but it is his» primary «sustenance, he recites» the «three blessings» of Grace after Meals, as he would after eating bread. The Gemara asks: «And is there a» vegetable «where in its boiled» state «it is» primary «sustenance? Rav Ashi said: This was taught» with regard to «a cabbage stalk,» which is nourishing.

moves.cueHe: רבי עקיבא אומר אפילו אכל שלק כו׳
moves.summary: takes up Rabbi Akiva's clause from the mishna
moves.about: the mishna's ruling that one who ate boiled vegetables as his sustenance recites the three blessings

moves.cueHe: ומי איכא מידי דהוה שלק מזוני
moves.summary: denies that any boiled vegetable is sustaining enough for the ruling to apply
moves.about: whether there is any boiled vegetable that can serve as a person's primary sustenance

moves.cueHe: אמר רב אשי: בקלח של כרוב שנו
moves.summary: names the cabbage stalk as the case the mishna has in mind
moves.about: there is such a vegetable — the mishna speaks of a cabbage stalk, which is nourishing
